subtopic: Series EE vs. Series I Savings Bonds
source_evidence: Series EE U.S. Savings Bonds are an appreciation-type (or accrual-type) savings security. Series I U.S. Savings Bonds are inflation-indexed.
answer: Series EE and Series I savings bonds are both sold at face value, and each has a $10,000 annual purchase limit (face value). Their main difference is how their interest is described: Series EE bonds are appreciation- or accrual-type securities, while Series I bonds are inflation-indexed and offer a fixed rate of interest adjusted for inflation. For either type, redeeming within the first five years means forfeiting the three most recent months’ interest; after five years, there is no redemption penalty.
